RESOLUTION.DESC:
The Security Council,
Acknowledging that “Liberate Utopia” served an essential purpose in helping [region]Utopia[/region]’s residents reclaim their region from rogues, at a time when the region lacked the means to do so itself, restoring [region]Utopia[/region]’s idyllic and positive environment,
Noting that the specific security concerns and administrative disruptions that prompted SC#13 to be written have been fully resolved by the region’s current residents and global circumstances,
Observing that no native population of [region]Utopia[/region] remains, its founding nations and long-standing residents before its refounding having long since ceased to exist, leaving only recently arrived nations with no historical claim to the region predating this Council’s original intervention,
Recognizing that the Security Council’s resolutions are meant to uphold durable principles rather than preserve dated concerns and grievances,
Reflecting that the vulnerability following the loss of [region]Utopia[/region]’s founder, [nation]Utopian thoughts[/nation], left the region genuinely exposed, and SC#13’s intervention played a real part in seeing it through that period,
Further reflecting that the circumstances behind the one-time occurrence belong to a specific chapter in [region]Utopia[/region]’s history that has since closed,
Noting further that the residents of [region]Utopia[/region] took matters into their own hands, refounding the region and entrusting it in their own community,
Aware that [region]Utopia[/region], like any other founderless region, can rely on established defender coalitions to defend itself, coordinated through networks such as Libcord, which monitor and respond to raids regardless of formal treaty ties or Security Council resolutions,
Understanding that this Council repeals liberation resolutions once a region has shown long-term stability and no longer requires active World Assembly intervention, as with the recent repeal of “Liberate Portugal de Esquerda,” where the resolution was recognized as unable to serve its intended function without a governor to enforce it, leaving the text ineffective without any active protective effort, and as with the repeal of “Liberate Syria,” where invading forces were found to no longer pose a threat to the region, as they were long gone,
Exhausted that “Liberate Utopia” has stood 17 years past the events that needed it, far longer than its original purpose,
Hereby repeals “Liberate Utopia”.
RESOLUTION.NAME: Repeal "Liberate Utopia"
